purpose: Resolve the SOURCE_CONFLICT inside the canonical forensic design artifact for phase QNTYLAB_AGENT_CONTEXT_PACKET_V0 (increment C1 of the CLOSED_PASS umbrella QNTYLAB_REPOSITORY_ERGONOMICS_AND_MODULARITY_CLEANUP_V0): forensic section 3 enumerates exactly 19 named packet fields while forensic section 4 line 89 states 'Fixed 20-field schema'. The extra table row '| *(envelope: keys, newlines, escaping)* | | | ~1,000 |' is byte-budget accounting for serialization overhead, not a packet field. This clarification resolves the conflict at the governance layer only; it changes no runtime code, no forensic artifact, no scientific authority, and no umbrella state.

source_conflict.description: The forensic design artifact contradicts itself on the packet field count. Section 3 (Packet field contract, line 45) says the packet has 'exactly these fields, in this order' and then enumerates exactly 19 named field rows. Section 4 (Sizing rules, line 89) says 'Fixed 20-field schema; renderer rejects unknown/missing fields.' The 20th item is the table row '| *(envelope: keys, newlines, escaping)* | | | ~1,000 |' (line 69), which has no field identifier, no content semantics, and no source semantics; it only accounts for ~1,000 bytes of serialization overhead (keys, newlines, escaping) already included in the total sizing. Counting it as a field is a counting error, not a design intent to add a twentieth semantic field.
exact_quotes: exactly these fields, in this order
Fixed 20-field schema; renderer rejects unknown/missing fields.

resolution.forbidden_field_names_note: No twentieth field is invented under any other name either: the authorized field set is exactly the 19 enumerated named fields and nothing else.

mechanical_reasoning: 1. Forensic section 3 says the packet has 'exactly these fields, in this order' and then enumerates a fixed ordered list of named field rows.

2. That enumeration contains exactly 19 named identifiers: REPOSITORY, HEAD, WORKTREE, PHASE_ID, STATE, OBJECTIVE, AUTHORITY_SOURCE, ALLOWED_OPERATIONS, FORBIDDEN_OPERATIONS, INPUT_CONTRACTS, OUTPUT_CONTRACTS, LOAD_BEARING_INVARIANTS, RELEVANT_CODE, RELEVANT_TESTS, IMMUTABLE_PATHS, OPEN_BLOCKERS, REVIEW_LIFECYCLE, NEXT_ACTION, VERIFY_COMMAND.
3. Every one of the 19 named rows carries both content semantics (what the field holds) and source semantics (where the value is derived from), so each is a genuine packet field.
4. The envelope row '| *(envelope: keys, newlines, escaping)* |' has neither a field identifier nor content/source semantics; it is typographically distinct (italicized, parenthesized, unnamed).
5. The envelope row describes serialization mechanics only: keys, newlines, and escaping.
6. The ~1,000-byte envelope amount is already included in the total sizing ('~ 5,090 B typical, <= 8,192 B hard cap'), i.e. it is overhead accounting, not packet state.
7. Therefore the envelope is formatting/byte overhead, not a packet field.
8. A twentieth semantic field would require new content and source semantics that are absent from the design target; inventing them would exceed the forensic design.
9. Choosing the enumerated named-field contract (19 fields) minimizes invention and preserves the section 3 guarantee of 'exactly these fields'.
